overview: Native gamepad support for Minecraft Java: analog movement, stick camera, and menu navigation that steps between real slots and buttons instead of shoving a pointer at them.
Client-side only. The server neither needs it nor knows about it.

1.2.2: The on-screen keyboard deletes again, and its cursor keys move the cursor.
1.2.1: The stick no longer starts a sprint in water, so crossing one does not put you face down.
The sprint button still swims, the way the keyboard does.
1.2.0: Pandorical's notice badge names your button, not a key.
1.1.4: Every action takes a pad control now, under Options > Controls > Key Binds: vanilla's, other mods', and Pandorical's slots alike.
Start clears a binding the way Escape clears a key, and what you change is kept.
Stepping through the hotbar is an action of its own, so the shoulders can do what only the scroll wheel could.
The pad shakes when you are hurt, land a hit, break a block, get a bite, or an explosion goes off near you.
It only shakes while the pad is the hands in use, so one left charging on the shelf stays quiet.
A settings page in Pandorical's mod menu: look and pointer speed, a deadzone for each stick, inverted look, and rumble with its strength.
Clicking into a text box brings up an on-screen keyboard: chat, an anvil, a book, a command block, the creative search.
A sign opens it the moment the sign is placed, so a pad can write one without reaching for the keys.
Holding the stick forward sprints without the view pulsing.
Vanilla ended the sprint on every bump, so the wider view flickered all the way up a hill.
Sneak moves to the stick click.
B opens chat with the pointer on the newest link, so accepting a teleport is B then A.
Button hints name the buttons printed on your own pad.
1.1.3: A button held over from a closing screen no longer jumps or sneaks.
B and Start close only what Escape would, and Y closes the inventory it opened.
A press just after a screen opens over the world is ignored.
Stick click actually sprints, and an offhand rod reels.
The shoulders scroll a list rather than the slot under the cursor.
Triggers let go a little below where they press.
1.1.0: The left trigger reels a fish by how far it is pulled.
1.0.1: Analog movement, stick camera, and menu navigation that snaps to what you meant.
Boat steering answers how far the stick is pushed, instead of turning as hard as it can.
